clue.text: Lay speculators in a state after losing pots ruinously

indicators.note: after losing says the letters of the word pots are taken away from the word speculators
ruinously says the word pots is wrecked, its letters scattered rather than in a block, before removal

explanation.surface: Gamblers on the markets end up in a state after losing their stakes disastrously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruinously' means the removed letters are scattered rather than a block: they come out as P, then TO, then S. 'in a state' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay, as in lay preacher, means not belonging to the clergy, which is the worldly, non-religious sense.

clue.text: Try to use dodgy guarantor

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters of try and use are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tries to rely on a shady person to vouch for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A surety is a person who takes responsibility for another's debt or obligation, i.e. a guarantor.

clue.text: Green alluvial flat

definitions.meaning: green here means inexperienced or naive
Chambers gives a dialect sense: a low-lying meadow liable to flooding, river-deposited land

explanation.surface: A description of a fresh green riverside meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow means youthfully inexperienced; it is also a rare dialect word for a low, flood-prone meadow.

clue.text: Not bright enough to tackle slur indirectly

indicators.note: indirectly means not straight, so the letters of tackle and slur are taken in a roundabout order

explanation.surface: Someone too dim to confront an insult except in a roundabout way.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacklustre literally means lacking sheen, so dull rather than shining.

clue.text: Peculiar game

definitions.meaning: peculiar means odd or strange, an informal British sense
a card game in which players collect sets and runs

explanation.surface: A strange sort of contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummy is informal British for odd, and is also the name of a card game.

clue.text: Provided far too much within dance

indicators.note: within says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: provided means gave
OTT is short for over the top, i.e. excessive

explanation.surface: Someone supplied an excessive amount of something at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is an old French court dance in moderate four-four time.

clue.text: As well as being surrounded by revolutionary guards, they are waiting for a conference!

definitions.text: they are waiting for a conference!

indicators.note: being surrounded by puts the short connective inside the scrambled guards
revolutionary suggests overturning, so the letters of guards are rearranged

parts.note: as well as means and

explanation.surface: Delegates hemmed in by rebel guards sit waiting for a summit to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' gives GRADUS. The conference is the conferring of a degree, not a meeting, which the exclamation mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Graduands are students about to graduate, awaiting the formal conferment of their degrees.

clue.text: Endorsement to cut tax is introduced

indicators.note: introduced means put inside the shortened tax
to cut means the tax word loses its last letter

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax

explanation.surface: An approval for a tax reduction is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT, value added tax, is the British sales tax; 'to cut' docks it to VA.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official stamp in a passport, an endorsement permitting entry.

clue.text: Generate wrong impression of a young person

indicators.note: a wrong impression of a word is a garbled version, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: To create a mistaken image of a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is someone aged thirteen to nineteen, an adolescent.

clue.text: Judge is in Paris getting one to marry

parts.note: est is the French for is
I is the Roman numeral one
to mate is to pair up or marry

explanation.surface: A judge is in Paris, finding someone to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity roughly is to estimate or reckon it.

clue.text: Souvenir of priest immersed in humanitarian charity

indicators.note: immersed in places the priest inside the charity's initials

parts.note: RC is the Red Cross
Eli is the priest of Shiloh in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A keepsake left by a clergyman who worked for an aid organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object kept as a reminder of the past, a memento.

clue.text: Way to check an official inquiry

parts.note: means is a way of doing something
test means check

explanation.surface: A method of verifying a formal investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the official investigation of a person's income to decide eligibility for state benefits.

clue.text: Store bully managed to take customers for a ride

definitions.text: to take customers for a ride
definitions.note: a phrase describing what the vehicle does, standing in for a noun

indicators.note: managed suggests something handled and reworked, so the letters of store and bully are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop bully succeeded in cheating customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take for a ride' suggests swindling; here it is literal. The definition is loose: it describes what the vehicle does rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolleybus is an electric bus fed from overhead wires that carries passengers on its route.

clue.text: Aromatic substance found in herbal medicine

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words herbal medicine

explanation.surface: A fragrant ingredient discovered in a herbal remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Balm is a fragrant soothing ointment or resin, a scented salve.

clue.text: He preaches that sin and remorse are not in order

indicators.note: not in order says the letters of sin and remorse are jumbled

explanation.surface: A preacher declares that sin and remorse are out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermoniser is one who delivers sermons, often moralising at length.

clue.text: Alienation from agreements not lacking substance

indicators.note: from is a weak signal that the letters are made out of, i.e. rearranged from, the fodder
lacking substance means the word not loses its middle, keeping only its ends

explanation.surface: Falling out after deals that did have some content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking substance' empties NOT to NT; 'from' then signals an anagram of AGREEMENTS plus NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangement is the state of being alienated or cut off from someone formerly close.

clue.text: Costume made initially to get a part performance

parts.note: rig is informal for an outfit or costume

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of made

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: Dressing up for a minor role in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, complicated procedure, a fuss, as in 'what a performance'.

clue.text: A sign of where swimmers are finally getting changed

indicators.note: finally getting changed means the last letter of the tank word is swapped for another

parts.note: fish swim in an aquarium

explanation.surface: A notice showing where swimmers get changed at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimmers are fish, not people; their tank's last letter is replaced, though the clue does not say by what.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquarius, the water carrier, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Definite deception inherent in strong promotion

parts.note: hard as in hard facts means definite
a sell is an old word for a hoax or deception

explanation.surface: Clear dishonesty built into aggressive advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard sell is aggressive, high-pressure salesmanship.

clue.text: A sad quagmire to engineer for a Sunday

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A sorry mess has been arranged for a weekend day.
explanation.definitionFit: Quadragesima is the first Sunday in Lent, about forty days before Easter.

clue.text: A form of convertible gold on deposit

indicators.note: in a down answer, on places the gold symbol after the deposit word

parts.note: to land is to set down or deposit
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A kind of convertible currency, gold, held in a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' suggests money; it is a car or carriage with a folding top.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled carriage or car whose top folds down.

clue.text: Censures poor investment in building society

indicators.note: investment in means the weak word is placed inside the society's initials

parts.note: BS is the abbreviation for building society, a British savings and mortgage lender
lame means poor or feeble

explanation.surface: Criticism of a bad investment with a building society.
explanation.definitionFit: To blame is to find fault with, which is to censure.

clue.text: Young lady removing outer clothing for attendant

indicators.note: removing outer clothing strips off the outside letters of the young lady word

parts.note: a maiden is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A young woman undressing in front of her servant.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant or helper, one who attends another.

clue.text: Tommy and Bobby make a big splash

parts.note: Tommy Cannon, one half of the British comedy double act Cannon and Ball
Bobby Ball, the other half of the act

explanation.surface: Two performers together create a sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: Cannon and Ball were a popular British TV comedy duo, Tommy Cannon and Bobby Ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannonball is a jump into water with knees hugged, made to throw up a big spray.

clue.text: Uproar heard from poet

indicators.note: heard says the word for uproar is taken by ear

parts.note: uproar means noise

explanation.surface: A clamour sounds out from a writer of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes was an English poet, best known for The Highwayman.

clue.text: Reveller half cut on drugs

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for a noun, a person taking drugs

indicators.note: half cut means the first half of the reveller word is chopped off; half-cut is also slang for drunk

parts.note: a carouser is a drunken reveller

explanation.surface: A partygoer, tipsy and high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' looks like British slang for tipsy but halves CAROUSER. The definition is loose: it means one who is on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for a habitual taker of illegal substances, an addict.

clue.text: Operation dreadfully toilsome to the right side of tummy

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of toilsome are scrambled
the right side of a written word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A surgical procedure, painfully laborious, on the right of the abdomen.
explanation.definitionFit: An ileostomy is surgery creating an opening from the ileum through the abdominal wall.

clue.text: Some without first experience holding party to be a scene of depravity

indicators.note: holding says the shortened word wraps around the party
without means the following letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of experience

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Some inexperienced people at a party turn out to be a den of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without first experience' removes E, the first letter of experience, from SOME; SOM then holds DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodom is the biblical city destroyed for its wickedness, a byword for corruption.

clue.text: Overturned records encourage ostentatious display

indicators.note: overturned means the records word is turned back to front

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records
to urge is to encourage

explanation.surface: Upset discs prompt a showy display.
explanation.definitionFit: A splurge is a lavish, showy spending spree or display of extravagance.

clue.text: Cricketer, who found acclaim with The Bat

definitions.text: who found acclaim with The Bat
definitions.meaning: Johann ... the Younger, whose operetta Die Fledermaus means The Bat

explanation.surface: A cricketer who won praise for his batting.
explanation.walkthrough: The bat suggests cricket, but The Bat is the operetta Die Fledermaus.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an England cricket captain and the Viennese composer of Die Fledermaus share this surname.
